what: Round 7, item (A): the cause of the processor-share subtest failing now and then on an unchanged kernel, as far as it was established, and the change made to the subtest.

probe.host_load: the later boots ran beside the mutant samples, which keep all eight logical processors busy

hypotheses: host or emulator slow: about fifty ticks, all of them the program's own, few rounds
another guest task or an interrupt storm: few own ticks, or many task switches
guest clock fast: far fewer than fifty ticks
conclusion: Established: the failures are reproduced on the unchanged kernel when the build machine is saturated by other work; in every failed run the program's rounds per tick of its own drop to about a tenth for some seconds while the ticks stay its own; with a guest clock that counts instructions every alone stretch holds the same count and the subtest passes. So the emulator's speed changes while the guest clock follows the host's. Not established: whether a given stall comes from the processors being taken or from the processor frequency dropping. Changed check: the subtest sets aside a measurement whose five stretches differ in rounds per own tick by more than a quarter, and measures again, five times at most; the pass conditions are unchanged; no steady measurement is a failure. The clock check is unchanged.
